newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan Kemano deal closer after bill unveiled.
newsitem.headline: Alcan Kemano deal closer after bill unveiled.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd said on Thursday that it moved closer to a settlement with British Columbia over its cancelled Kemano hydroelectric project after the province introduced enabling legislation.

Alcan spokesman Ray Castelli said the legislation, introduced on Wednesday before the legislature recessed for the summer, would give the government authority to enter into an agreement to sell power to Alcan.
Discussions have focused on the province selling power to Alcan at the same cost as if the Kemano plant had gone into operation. The legislation paves the way for such a contract.

The government ordered the half-built project scrapped in 1995 after the aluminium company had spent C$535 million on it. Kemano was intended to provide power to Alcan's Kitimat smelter in British Columbia, its largest smelter in the world.

Castelli said the enabling legislation removed one stumbling block to a deal and was welcomed by the company, especially after reports that the government was considering legislation to impose a settlement.
"This is good legislation. We support this legislation. It brings us one step closer," he said.

British Columbia Premier Glen Clark said earlier this week that the two sides were making progress toward a deal and an agreement might be possible by today. Officials said that now appeared unlikely but remained optimistic about the prospects.

Local media have reported that an expansion at Kitimat would cost at least C$1 billion and create at least 350 permanent jobs. Castelli said Alcan had not drafted any specific plans for an expansion but that any project would likely cost at least C$1 billion.
